rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the majority together around a narrow, Yates-style contextual reading tethering §1512(c)(2) to evidence-impairment, with Barrett or Gorsuch as plausible alternatives if the Chief prefers to manage assignments or if the opinion leans more textualist/lenity-focused. Kagan is the most likely principal dissenter emphasizing the distinct object/verbs and a stringent reading of “corruptly,” with Alito likely to add or join a separate dissent stressing grammar/surplusage and Sotomayor more likely to join than write.
